questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The volume of a closed reaction vessel in which the following equilibrium reaction occurs is halved :
$2 \mathrm{SO}_{2}(\mathrm{~g})+\mathrm{O}_{2}(\mathrm{~g}) \rightleftharpoons 2 \mathrm{SO}_{3}(\mathrm{~g})$
As a result,
options: The rates of forward and backward reactions will remain the same.
The equilibrium will shift to the right.
The rate of forward reaction will become double that of reverse reaction and the equilibrium will shift to the right.
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{c}}=\frac{\left[\mathrm{SO}_{3}\right]^{2}}{\left[\mathrm{SO}_{2}\right]^{2}\left[\mathrm{O}_{2}\right]}$
If volume is reduced to half, $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{c}}$ will decrease to half. Thus, to maintain the equilibrium, the reaction should shift in the forward direction, i.e. towards right. Also, to attain equilibrium back, the rate of forward direction will become double the rate of backward direction.

options: Create potential difference between the two electrodes
Remove adsorbed oxygen from electrode surfaces
questions.solution:
In hydrogen-oxygen fuel cell, following reactions take place to create potential difference between the two electrodes.

\begin{array}{c}
2 \mathrm{H}_{2}(\mathrm{~g})+4 \mathrm{OH}^{-}(\mathrm{aq}) \rightarrow 4 \mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}(\mathrm{l})+4 \mathrm{e}^{-} \\
\mathrm{O}_{2}(\mathrm{~g})+2 \mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}(\mathrm{l})+4 \mathrm{e}^{-} \rightarrow 4 \mathrm{OH}^{-}(\mathrm{aq}) \\
\hline \text { Overall reaction }=2 \mathrm{H}_{2}(\mathrm{~g})+\mathrm{O}_{2}(\mathrm{~g}) \rightarrow 2 \mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}(\mathrm{l})
\end{array}

the net reaction is the same as burning (combustion) of hydrogen to form water.

questions.q: A circle has radius 3 and its centre lies on the line $y=x-1$. The equation of the circle, if it passes through $(7,3)$, is
questions.solution:
Let the centre of the circle be $(h, k)$. Since the centre lies on the line $y=x-1\therefore k=h-1 ......(i)$
Since the circle passes through the point $(7,3)$, therefore, the distance of the centre from this point is the radius of the circle.
$\therefore \quad 3=\sqrt{(h-7)^{2}+(k-3)^{2}}\Rightarrow \quad 3=\sqrt{(h-7)^{2}+(h-1-3)^{2}}\Rightarrow \quad h=7$ or $h=4$
For $h=7$, we get $k=6$ and for $h=4$, we get $k=3$
Hence, the circles which satisfy the given conditions are:
$(x-7)^{2}+(y-6)^{2}=9$
or $x^{2}+y^{2}-14 x+12 y+76=0$
and $(x-4)^{2}+(y-3)^{2}=9$ or

x^{2}+y^{2}-8 x-6 y+16=0

questions.q: If $\omega=\frac{-1+\sqrt{3} i}{2}$ then $\left(3+\omega+3 \omega^{2}\right)^{4}$ is
questions.solution:
Let $\omega=\frac{-1+\sqrt{3} i}{2}$
Now, $1+\omega+\omega^{2}=0$, and $\omega^{3}=1$
then $\left(3+\omega+3 \omega^{2}\right)^{4}=\left(3+\omega+3 \omega^{2}+2 \omega-2 \omega\right)^{4}$
\begin{array}{l}
=\left(3+3 \omega+3 \omega^{2}-2 \omega\right)^{4}=\left[3\left(1+2+\omega^{2}\right)-2 \omega\right]^{4} \\
=(0-2 \omega)^{4}=16 \omega^{4}=16 \omega \quad\left(\because \omega^{3}=1\right)
\end{array}

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Let $f$ be the function defined by
$f(x)=\left\{\begin{array}{ll}
\frac{x^{2}-1}{x^{2}-2|x-1|-1}, & x \neq 1 \\
1 / 2, & x=1
\end{array}\right.$
options: The function is continuous for all values of $\mathrm{x}$
The function is continuous only for $x \gt 1$
The function is not continuous at $x=1$
questions.solution:
For $x \lt  1, f(x)=\frac{x^{2}-1}{x^{2}+2 x-3}=\frac{x+1}{x+3}\therefore \lim _{x \rightarrow 1^{-}} f(x)=\frac{1}{2}$
For $x \gt 1, f(x)=\frac{x^{2}-1}{x^{2}-2 x+1}=\frac{x+1}{x-1}$
\therefore \lim _{\mathrm{x} \rightarrow 1^{+}} \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=\infty

$\therefore$ the function is not continuous at $x=1$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The value of the integral $\int_{-1}^{3}(|x|+|x-1|) d x$ is
questions.solution:
We have

|x|+|x-1|=\left\{\begin{array}{c}
-x-(x-1)=-2 x+1, \text { if } x \leq 0 \\
x-(x-1)=1, \text { if } 0 \leq x \leq 1 \\
x+x-1=2 x-1, \text { if } x \geq 1
\end{array}\right.

\begin{aligned}
& \therefore \int_{-1}^{3}(|x|+|x-1|) d x \\
=& \int_{-1}^{0}(-2 x+1) d x+\int_{0}^{1} 1 d x+\int_{1}^{3}(2 x-1) d x \\
=&\left[-x^{2}+x\right]_{-1}^{0}+[x]_{0}^{1}+\left[x^{2}-x\right]_{1}^{3}=9
\end{aligned}

questions.q: Value of $\int_{\pi / 6}^{\pi / 3} \frac{1}{1+\sqrt{\cot x}} d x$ is
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} \mathrm{I} &=\int_{\pi / 6}^{\pi / 3} \frac{1}{1+\sqrt{\cot x}} \mathrm{dx} \\ &=\int_{\pi / 6}^{\pi / 3} \frac{\sqrt{\sin x}}{\sqrt{\sin x}+\sqrt{\cos x}} \mathrm{dx} \end{aligned} ......(i)$
Then, $\mathrm{I}=\int_{\pi / 6}^{\pi / 3} \frac{\sqrt{\sin \left(\frac{\pi}{2}-\mathrm{x}\right)}}{\sqrt{\sin \left(\frac{\pi}{2}-\mathrm{x}\right)}+\sqrt{\cos \left(\frac{\pi}{2}-\mathrm{x}\right)}} \mathrm{dx}\Rightarrow \mathrm{I}=\int_{\pi / 6}^{\pi / 3} \frac{\sqrt{\cos \mathrm{x}}}{\sqrt{\cos \mathrm{x}}+\sqrt{\sin \mathrm{x}}} \mathrm{dx} ......(ii)$
Adding (i) and (ii), we get

\begin{array}{l}
2 \mathrm{I}=\int_{\pi / 6}^{\pi / 3} \frac{\sqrt{\sin \mathrm{x}}+\sqrt{\cos \mathrm{x}}}{\sqrt{\cos \mathrm{x}}+\sqrt{\sin \mathrm{x}}} \mathrm{dx} \\
\Rightarrow 2 \mathrm{I}=\int_{\pi / 6}^{\pi / 3} 1 \cdot \mathrm{dx}=[\mathrm{x}]_{\pi / 6}^{\pi / 3}=\frac{\pi}{3}-\frac{\pi}{6}=\frac{\pi}{6} \Rightarrow \mathrm{I}=\pi / 12
\end{array}

questions.q: Evaluate $\lim _{x \rightarrow 2} \frac{\sqrt{(x+7)}-3 \sqrt{(2 x-3)}}{\sqrt[3]{(x+6)}-2 \sqrt[3]{(3 x-5)}}$.
questions.solution:
We have

L=\lim _{x \rightarrow 2} \frac{\sqrt{(x+7)}-3 \sqrt{(2 x-3)}}{\sqrt[3]{(x+6)}-2 \sqrt[3]{(3 x-5)}}\left(\frac{0}{0} \text { form }\right)

Let $x-2=t$ such that when $x \rightarrow 2, t \rightarrow 0$. Then

\begin{array}{l}
L=\lim _{t \rightarrow 0} \frac{(t+9)^{\frac{1}{2}}-3(2 t+1)^{\frac{1}{2}}}{(t+8)^{\frac{1}{3}}-2(3 t+1)^{\frac{1}{3}}} \quad\left(\frac{0}{0} \text { form }\right) \\
=\frac{3}{2} \lim _{t \rightarrow 0} \frac{\left(1+\frac{t}{9}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}-(2 t+1)^{\frac{1}{2}}}{\left(1+\frac{t}{8}\right)^{\frac{1}{3}}-(3 t+1)^{\frac{1}{3}}} \quad\left(\frac{0}{0} \text { form }\right) \\
=\frac{3}{2} \lim _{t \rightarrow 0} \frac{\frac{1}{2} \frac{t}{9}-(2 t) \frac{1}{2}-(3 t) \frac{1}{3}}{3}=\frac{3}{2} \frac{1}{\frac{18}{2}}-1=\frac{1}{24}-1 \quad 23
\end{array}

questions.q:
If vector equation of the line $\frac{x-2}{2}=\frac{2 y-5}{-3}=z+1$, is
$\overrightarrow{\mathrm{r}}=\left(2 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+\frac{5}{2} \hat{\mathrm{j}}-\hat{\mathrm{k}}\right)+\lambda\left(2 \hat{\mathrm{i}}-\frac{3}{2} \hat{\mathrm{j}}+\mathrm{p} \hat{\mathrm{k}}\right)$ then $\mathrm{p}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
The given line is $\frac{x-2}{2}=\frac{2 y-5}{-3}=z+1$,

\Rightarrow \quad \frac{x-2}{2}=\frac{y-\frac{5}{2}}{-\frac{3}{2}}=\frac{z+1}{0}

This shows that the given line passes through the point $\left(2, \frac{5}{2},-1\right)$ and has direction ratios $\left(2, \frac{-3}{2}, 0\right)$. Thus, given line passes through the point having position vector $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}=2 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+\frac{5}{2} \hat{\mathrm{j}}-\hat{\mathrm{k}}$ and is parallel to the vector $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}=\left(2 \hat{\mathrm{i}}-\frac{3}{2} \hat{\mathrm{j}}-0 \hat{\mathrm{k}}\right) \cdot$ So, its vector equation is $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{r}}=\left(2 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+\frac{5}{2} \hat{\mathrm{j}}-\hat{\mathrm{k}}\right)+\lambda\left(2 \hat{\mathrm{i}}-\frac{3}{2} \hat{\mathrm{j}}-0 \hat{\mathrm{k}}\right)$ 
Hence, $\mathrm{p}=0$

questions.q: If the differential equation for a simple harmonic motion is $\frac{d^{2} y}{d t^{2}}+2 y=0$, the time-period of the motion is
questions.solution:
The differential equation of simple harmonic motion is

\frac{d^{2} y}{d t^{2}}+2 y=0 \text { or } \frac{d^{2} y}{d t^{2}}=-2 y......(i)

Standard equation of simple harmonic motion is

\frac{d^{2} y}{d t^{2}}=-\omega^{2} y......(ii)

Comparing eq. (i) and (ii), $\omega^{2}=2$ or $\omega=\sqrt{2}$
As we know, $\omega=\frac{2 \pi}{T}\therefore$ Time period, $T=\frac{2 \pi}{\omega}=\frac{2 \pi}{\sqrt{2}}=\pi \sqrt{2} \mathrm{sec}$
